Subject: Discovery recap: Inference cost pressure & next steps (FinTechCorp)

Hi Alex / Samir —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap to make sure we captured everything correctly and to outline proposed next steps. I summarized the items you called out and what success looks like for FinTechCorp below. Please flag any corrections.

TL;DR: primary goal is to reduce per-API-call inference cost by ~3x while keeping p99 latency <= 200ms for customer-facing scoring endpoints. You're open to model quantization and batching/caching approaches, but need to validate latency and MLP/regulatory constraints.

Key pain points and background
- Heavy usage for real-time scoring (fraud/risk models) driving high per-token costs; current monthly spend on inference estimated at ~$85k.
- Current stack: in-house Triton on k8s, using AWS p3 instances for heavy CUDA workloads; orchestration overhead and inefficient batching hurting unit economics.
- Latency SLOs: p50 ~ 50-80ms, p99 spike up to 600-800ms during peak; target is p99 <= 200ms for scoring flows.
- Embeddings-heavy workflows for search/recommendation also contribute to cost.
- Procurement constraints: need clear unit cost/cost-savings justification and standard security artifacts (SOC2, data residency statement).

Success criteria (what FinTechCorp needs to see)
- 2.5–3x reduction in per-query inference costs for production scoring (including amortized infra and token counts).
- Maintain or improve p99 latency to <= 200ms for scoring endpoints at expected QPS (see QPS below).
- Clear migration plan with minimal impact to customers and rollback strategy.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 report, KMS integration, and audit logging for requests.

Technical details you shared
- Target production QPS (peak): 120–150 TPS across a 3-region footprint; typical request sizes ~80–250 tokens.
- Desired batching behavior: small batches preferred for latency-sensitive endpoints (batch size 8–32), larger batches acceptable for offline/embedding workloads.
- Cache opportunities: prefix/KV caching for long-lived session contexts estimated to save ~20–25% of tokens if applied.
- Quantization: team is open to int8/4-bit if accuracy loss is <1% on key model metrics; willing to run A/B validation.

Proposed next steps
1) We will run a short technical POC: Redwood will replicate a production-like workload (subset) to measure unit economics under different serving configs (batching, quantization). Please share sample anonymized logs or token/call histograms and current monthly inference spend.
2) Schedule a deep-dive with your infra lead (Samir) to align on network/topology and security requirements — propose Wed 2026-04-22 10:00am PT.
3) Procurement: attach initial commercial deck and inference-cost-template (attached). We'll provide an initial cost comparison and a draft mutual action plan for procurement review.

Attachments: redwood-discovery-recap.pdf, inference-cost-template.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the POC onboarding once you share logs.

Best,
Ben Carter
